_meta.note: Turn two research-adapter test ideas into runnable, wired harnesses over the ALREADY-SHIPPED adapter (ground-check / stamp-evidence / research-context). These are characterization/red-team proofs: teeth = they go RED if the code regresses or a boundary claim is false. (RT) Red-team the gate/review BOUNDARY — a committed corpus that plants every mechanical failure mode (FABRICATED-QUOTE / UNGROUNDED / MISSING-SOURCE / STALE) PLUS two grounded-but-wrong claims (a paraphrase that overreaches its real excerpt; a real excerpt quoted out of context). The deterministic proof asserts ground-check catches all MECHANICAL fabrication and stays SILENT on truth (the two grounded-but-wrong claims report `grounded`), node ≡ python. The phase is review-gated: a distinct actor, seeded by `hb-audit --questions`, must independently identify the two grounded-but-wrong claims the gate passed — proving the review layer closes the semantic gap. Grounding != truth, made testable. (SC) Scale + parity — a DETERMINISTIC seeded generator builds a large messy corpus (60 sources, 200 claims, unicode, line-wraps, multi-claim-per-source, 4 sections); the proof asserts ground-check + research-context are node ≡ python BYTE-identical at scale, stamp-evidence produces the same map, the run completes within a timeout ceiling, and the grounded/issue counts are honest — catching the encoding/sort/perf divergences the toy fixtures hide. Proof-driven: spec-first, gated, refuted; each harness wired into the suite and documented as a method.

phases.title: Red-team the gate/review boundary (grounding catches fabrication, stays silent on truth)

tasks.title: Spec-first: red-team corpus + the classification/boundary proof
tasks.description: Author the committed red-team fixture under plugin/adapters/research/fixtures/redteam/ : evidence.json + sources/ with EIGHT claims exercising the whole boundary — c_ok (grounded clean), c_fab (FABRICATED-QUOTE: excerpt not in source), c_nosrc (UNGROUNDED: source undeclared), c_noex (UNGROUNDED: empty excerpt), c_missing (MISSING-SOURCE: source s_missing declared but plugin/adapters/research/fixtures/redteam/sources/s_missing.txt absent), c_stale (STALE: source s_stale with a deliberately WRONG recorded sha256), and the two GROUNDED-BUT-WRONG cases the gate cannot judge: c_drift (a real excerpt present in its source, but `text` overreaches it — mark the text with the token OVERREACH) and c_context (a real excerpt present in a secondary source, quoted out of context — mark the text with the token OUT-OF-CONTEXT). Grounded sources (s1, s_blog) are shaless so they ground via excerpt. Expected: ground-check reports grounded=3 issues=5, and c_drift/c_context are in the grounded set (never flagged). Author the proof docs/howto/gate-examples/ground-check-redteam.sh (prints `RED-TEAM-OK grounded=3 issues=5`): assert the exact grounded/issue counts, that each mechanical defect id appears with its expected class, that c_drift and c_context do NOT appear in any issue line (the gate stays silent on truth), and that ground-check is node ≡ python on the red-team corpus. The proof characterizes existing ground-check; its teeth are the exact classification (a regression that over- or under-flags, or that starts judging truth, turns it RED).

phases.title: Scale + parity — the adapter stays node ≡ python and fast on a large messy corpus

tasks.title: Spec-first: the scale-parity proof (RED before the generator exists)
tasks.description: Author the proof docs/howto/gate-examples/research-scale-parity.sh (prints `SCALE-PARITY-OK sources=60 claims=200 grounded=160 issues=40`) RED-first — it references a not-yet-existing generator, so it FAILS now. Contract the proof asserts: generate a large corpus into a temp dir via the generator; ground-check node ≡ python BYTE-identical on it and reports `grounded=160 issues=40`; research-context node ≡ python byte-identical for each of the four sections (background/method/results/discussion); stamp-evidence node ≡ python produce the SAME map (canonicalized parsed-equal); the ground-check run completes within a `timeout` ceiling (a perf guard against an accidental O(n^2) blowup); then print the marker with the scale/counts. mktemp lives in the PROOF (not a gate criterion). The heavy scale teeth ride on this proof's structured marker line.

tasks.title: Implement the deterministic large-corpus generator (make the proof green)
tasks.description: Implement plugin/adapters/research/fixtures/scale/gen.js — a DETERMINISTIC, seeded-by-index generator (no time / no randomness) that writes evidence.json + sources/ to an output dir arg. 60 sources (s_00..s_59), 200 claims (c_000..c_199, ZERO-PADDED so node and python string-sort identically), source = i % 60, section = [background,method,results,discussion][i%4]. Every 5th claim (i%5==0) is FABRICATED (excerpt a NOTINSOURCE-<i> token absent from the source) -> 40 fabricated / 160 grounded. Two-pass: assign claims, then build each source's .txt from the grounded excerpts that cite it (plus filler and unicode °C / » / é / — ) with a synthetic line-wrap injected into each stored excerpt (so whitespace normalization is exercised) while the claim keeps a single-space excerpt. Sources are shaless (ground via excerpt; no STALE). Result: ground-check reports grounded=160 issues=40 deterministically. Make docs/howto/gate-examples/research-scale-parity.sh green; keep tests/parity.sh green.

review.prompt: Refute that RT is done. (1) Harness soundness: does ground-check-redteam.sh have TEETH — would it go RED if ground-check stopped catching a fabrication, or started flagging a grounded-but-wrong claim (mutation-test it)? Are the counts (grounded=3 issues=5) and per-class assertions real, and is node ≡ python actually checked on the red-team corpus? (2) THE BOUNDARY, exercised for real: independently of the gate, run `node plugin/templates/hb-audit.js planning/research-adapter-testing.dag.json --questions GATE_RT`, read plugin/adapters/research/fixtures/redteam/ , and identify WHICH claims are grounded-but-wrong (a real excerpt that does not support the paraphrase / is out of context). You must find c_drift and c_context — the gate reports them grounded; the review is what catches them. If you cannot, the red-team corpus or the boundary claim is weak. (3) Does the how-to state honestly that it verifies grounding, NOT truth, and that the refutation (seeded by --questions) is what closes the gap — no overclaim? (4) node/python/parity/prose/self-audit/skill-integrity green with T114 wired?
